chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"A single Iqamah without Adhan suffices for you when you are alone in your house."

And all these narrations indicate the emphasis of the Adhan in congregational prayer, because they include the permissibility of leaving it, restricted to the state of solitude and being alone, and this is not except for the individual. As for the specificity of Fajr and Maghrib, what indicates it has already passed, and what adds to its clarification is what he narrated:

key_terms.إِقَامَةٌ: Iqamah (the second call to prayer, signaling the start of prayer)

ai.seo_question: Is Adhan required when praying alone at home according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi uses this report from Abu Abdillah (al-Sadiq) to establish the Adhan as a recommended act (mustahabb) for congregational prayer, deducing this from the specific permission to omit it only during solitary prayer (al-wahd). This scholarly inference highlights the Adhan's role in distinguishing communal worship from private devotion, while noting that the specific emphasis on Fajr and Maghrib is supported by prior textual evidence.
